summary_plain: The SAFFIRE-II investigation burned solid materials like PMMA, Nomex, SIBAL, and silicone inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo spacecraft after it left the International Space Station. Researchers studied how these materials burn in microgravity to see how well terrestrial fire standards apply to spacecraft environments. This work is essential for improving fire safety on future long-duration space missions.
summary_expert: SAFFIRE-II conducted 9 tests using solid fuels including PMMA, PMMA plus Nomex, SIBAL, and silicone. Sample materials were tested in sheet geometries measuring 5 by 29 cm, with sample thicknesses ranging from 0.27 to 10 mm over 7 tests. Tests were performed with oxygen levels ranging from 21.5 to 22.1 percent (mole fraction 0.21 to 0.22) and a forced air flow speed (ventilation velocity) of 20 cm/s, with flow direction and sample thickness acting as varying parameters. The documents provided describe the objectives, design, and experimental parameters only, with flame spread rates ranging from 2.1 to 2.6 mm/s over 2 tests and burn times ranging from 115 to 900 s over 5 tests.

key_findings.text: The oxygen levels in SAFFIRE-II tests ranged from 21.5 to 22.1 percent.
The forced air flow speed in SAFFIRE-II tests was 20 cm/s.
The flame spread rate in SAFFIRE-II ranged from 2.1 to 2.6 mm/s over 2 tests.
The burn time in SAFFIRE-II ranged from 115 to 900 s over 5 tests.
The sample thickness in SAFFIRE-II ranged from 0.27 to 10 mm over 7 tests.
